title_en: Yu Zuomin et al. (8 persons) — case of illegal control, illegal detention, harboring, obstruction of official duties, and bribery
keywords_en: criminal; illegal control; illegal detention; harboring; obstructing official duties; bribery; first instance; intermediate people's court; Tianjin City; natural person; criminal law; identification of illegal control act; identification of illegal detention act; identification of harboring act; identification of obstructing official duties act; identification of bribery act
full_text_en:
Yu Zuomin et al. (8 persons) — illegal control, illegal detention, harboring, obstruction of official duties, and bribery

Defendant: Yu Zuomin, male, 63 years old, former Chairman of the Board of Directors of Tianjin Jinghai County Daqiuzhuang Enterprise Group Corporation, arrested on April 21, 1993.

Defendant: Yu Shaozheng, male, 25 years old, former General Manager of Tianjin Jinghai County Daqiuzhuang Enterprise Group Corporation, arrested on June 15, 1993.

Defendant: Liu Yonghua, male, 36 years old, former Acting General Manager of Tianjin Jinghai County Daqiuzhuang Wanquan Group Company, arrested on June 12, 1993.

Defendant: Zhou Kewen, male, 40 years old, former Director of the Security Committee of Tianjin Jinghai County Daqiuzhuang Enterprise Group Corporation, arrested on June 12, 1993.

Defendant: Ma Deshui, male, 38 years old, former Deputy General Manager of Tianjin Jinghai County Daqiuzhuang Wanquan Group Company and concurrently Factory Director of Quanfen Hot Rolled Strip Steel Plant, arrested on June 12, 1993.

Defendant: Huang Naiqi, male, 35 years old, former Manager of Tianjin Jinghai County Daqiuzhuang Wanquan Group Company International Trade Industrial Co., Ltd., arrested on June 12, 1993.

Defendant: Chen Guanghong, male, 37 years old, former Manager of the Qiugang Joint Venture Company in Haizhu District, Guangzhou, under Daqiuzhuang Yaoshun Group Company, Tianjin Jinghai County, arrested on June 12, 1993.

Defendant: Shi Jiaming, female, 38 years old, former Vice Chairman of the Board and Secretary-General of Tianjin Jinghai County Daqiuzhuang Enterprise Group Corporation, surrendered on April 17, 1993, arrested on July 16, 1993.

The eight defendants, including Yu Zuomin, were indicted by the Tianjin Branch of the People's Procuratorate to the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court on charges of jointly or individually committing the crimes of illegal control, illegal detention, harboring, obstruction of official duties, and bribery. The Tianjin Intermediate People's Court, after public trial, found the following facts:

On April 11, 1990, in Daqiuzhuang Village, Jinghai County, Tianjin, a case occurred where Liu Yutian was beaten to death by villagers Yu Zuoxiang and six others (all convicted). After this incident, the defendant Yu Zuomin instructed the responsible persons of various units affiliated with Daqiuzhuang to terminate the employment of Liu Yutian's relatives Liu Jingang, Liu Jinhui, Liu Jingong, and others, and dispatched personnel to monitor Liu Yutian's wife Yu Rongtian and children Liu Jinhui, Liu Jingang, Liu Jingong, Liu Jinyun, Liu Jinmin, forbidding them from leaving the village. This illegal control was not lifted until December 1992.

In the afternoon of November 27, 1992, over twenty teachers and students from the Cadre School of the Third Bureau of the Beijing State Security Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Cadre School) were visiting the Botong Store in Daqiuzhuang. Student Zhang Xinze and others argued with the store manager over prices and were taken away by Daqiuzhuang security personnel to the Security Joint Defense Team. Upon learning of this, defendant Zhou Kewen sent personnel to escort over ten students to the Security Committee. Zhou Kewen took the lead in beating teachers Cheng Gang and student Zhou Jianyi, among others. Those present joined in, kicking and punching the students. At around 4 p.m., after receiving a report from Zhou Kewen, defendant Yu Zuomin instructed Zhou Kewen to bring Cheng Gang to the meeting room on the third floor of the headquarters building. Yu Zuomin, along with defendants Yu Shaozheng, Zhou Kewen, and Shi Jiaming, questioned and verbally abused Cheng Gang. Shi Jiaming pulled Cheng Gang's hair, and Yu Shaozheng slapped Cheng Gang. Thereafter, Yu Zuomin had student Zhang Xinze brought to the meeting room for interrogation. At Yu Zuomin's prompting, Yu Shaozheng and others beat Zhang Xinze, causing a perforated left eardrum. At about 9 p.m., under pressure from the relevant authorities to release the detainees, Yu Zuomin forced Cheng Gang to write a "letter of repentance" under duress before releasing the unlawfully detained teachers and students. During the detention, fifteen persons, including Cheng Gang and Zhou Jianyi, were beaten and injured. Forensic examination confirmed that Zhang Xinze's left ear injury constituted a minor injury.

In late November 1992, defendant Yu Zuomin suspected that the former Daqiuzhuang Huada Group Company had economic problems and decided to have other companies review the enterprises affiliated with the Huada Group. On December 2, defendant Liu Yonghua sent personnel to bring Tian Yizheng, the factory director of the former Huada Group Oxygen Plant, to the Wanquan Group Company for unlawful detention and interrogation. On the afternoon of December 7, Yu Zuomin presided over an unlawful interrogation of Tian Yizheng in the meeting room on the third floor of the headquarters building, with over twenty participants including Liu Yonghua, Zhou Kewen, and Shi Jiaming. Yu Zuomin first slapped Tian Yizheng. Liu Yonghua, Zhou Kewen, Shi Jiaming, and the others then kicked and punched Tian Yizheng, stripped off his shirt, and struck him with an electric baton. The unlawful interrogation and beating lasted two hours. Subsequently, Yu Zuomin ordered Tian Yizheng to be taken back to Wanquan Group Company for continued unlawful detention, which was not terminated until December 15.

On the afternoon of December 4, 1992, defendant Yu Zuomin presided over an unlawful interrogation of Hou Hongbin, the former Deputy General Manager of Huada Group Company, in the meeting room on the third floor of the headquarters building. Over ten persons, including Yu Shaozheng and Shi Jiaming, participated. Yu Zuomin and Yu Shaozheng beat Hou Hongbin, and others present also kicked and punched him. At about 7 p.m. that day, Yu Zuomin ordered defendant Zhou Kewen to take Hou Hongbin to the Security Committee for detention. During the detention, Zhou Kewen conducted unlawful interrogations of Hou Hongbin. Yu Zuomin, Yu Shaozheng, and Shi Jiaming also conducted another unlawful interrogation of Hou Hongbin on the morning of December 13. The unlawful detention and interrogation of Hou Hongbin lasted until January 14, 1993.

At around 4 p.m. on December 8, 1992, defendant Yu Zuomin presided over an unlawful interrogation of Song Bao, the farm manager of the former Huada Group Company, in the meeting room on the third floor of the headquarters building. Yu Shaozheng, Zhou Kewen, and Shi Jiaming participated. Zhou Kewen, Shi Jiaming, and over ten others present also verbally abused and beat Song Bao. At about 6 p.m., Yu Zuomin ordered Song Bao to be taken to a farm under the Yaoshun Group Company for detention and interrogation. On December 10, defendant Liu Yonghua had Song Bao taken to Wanquan Group Company for detention. The unlawful detention of Song Bao was not lifted until January 15, 1993. During this period, Liu Yonghua also conducted unlawful interrogations of Song Bao.

On December 13, 1992, Wei Fuhe, a worker from the farm of the former Daqiuzhuang Huada Group Company, was beaten to death by Liu Yunzhang, Li Zhenbiao, Chen Xiangqi, Liu Shaosheng, and 14 others (all handled in separate cases), who were managers or employees of the Wanquan Group Company. After defendant Liu Yonghua reported this to Yu Zuomin, Yu Zuomin instructed Liu Yonghua to select several reliable persons to bear the blame. Liu Yonghua then assembled Liu Yunzhang, Li Zhenbiao, Chen Xiangqi, and Liu Shaosheng to coordinate their stories and fabricate lies in an attempt to conceal the truth, implying that others should deny having participated in the beating of Wei Fuhe. On the morning of December 14, upon learning that the public security authorities had identified Liu Yunzhang, Li Zhenbiao, Chen Xiangqi, and Liu Shaosheng as primary suspects, Yu Zuomin instructed Liu Yonghua to arrange for these four persons to flee. Liu Yonghua gave each of them RMB 20,000 to facilitate their escape. Later, fearing that Liu Yunzhang and the others might be easily discovered while hiding outside, Yu Zuomin decided to have them return to the village and hide. On December 15, Liu Yonghua, together with defendant Ma Deshui, brought Liu Yunzhang and the others back to the village and concealed them. On February 16, 1993, Liu Yonghua instructed Ma Deshui to hide Chen Xiangqi and Liu Shaosheng in Ma Deshui's home. The next day, when police and procuratorial officers were about to enter the village to search for Liu Yunzhang and the others, Yu Zuomin, knowing that they were hiding in the village, provided false information to the officers and delayed them, causing Liu Yunzhang and the others not to be captured. On February 20, Liu Yonghua, through Ma Deshui, gave Liu Yunzhang and the others an additional RMB 20,000 each and sent a car to take Liu Shaosheng to Xian County, Hebei Province, to hide. On March 1, Liu Yonghua sent a car, driven by defendant Chen Guanghong, to take Chen Xiangqi to Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, to hide. On March 11, Liu Yonghua, Ma Deshui, and defendant Huang Naiqi conspired, and Huang Naiqi hid Liu Yunzhang and Li Zhenbiao in the gantry crane machine room of the Quanfen Hot Rolled Strip Steel Plant. On March 14, Liu Yonghua again gave Liu Yunzhang and Li Zhenbiao RMB 20,000 each, and Huang Naiqi drove them to Hebei, Jiangsu, and other places to hide.

On the evening of December 15, 1992, defendant Yu Zuomin received a report from defendant Zhou Kewen that six public security officers, including Song Yiguang, had conducted an inspection of the scene of Wei Fuhe's death. Yu Zuomin ordered that Song Yiguang and the others be detained. Zhou Kewen immediately directed patrol officers from the Security Committee to detain Song Yiguang and the others on the third-floor corridor of the inspection site, cutting off their contact with the outside world. At around 8 a.m. on December 16, Song Yiguang and the others were taken to the headquarters meeting room. Yu Zuomin made baseless accusations against them. At about 11 a.m., under pressure from the Tianjin city leaders' instruction to "release them immediately," Yu Zuomin released Song Yiguang and the others. Yu Zuomin and Zhou Kewen unlawfully detained Song Yiguang and the others for 13 hours, seriously obstructing the lawful performance of duties by public security officers.

On February 16, 1993, the Tianjin public security and procuratorial authorities organized officers to prepare to enter Daqiuzhuang to search for Liu Yunzhang and the other four. Upon learning of this, defendant Yu Zuomin convened an emergency meeting that night to devise methods to obstruct the officers from carrying out their duties and ordered defendant Zhou Kewen to have personnel guard the village entrances. Zhou Kewen immediately assembled the security chiefs of various group companies under the headquarters to deploy measures. On the morning of February 17, Yu Zuomin led and directed others to surround and accuse the leaders of the public security and procuratorial authorities and the responsible person of Jinghai County who had entered Daqiuzhuang, obstructing the lawful activities of the officers in searching for Liu Yunzhang and the others and posting arrest warrants. At about 4 p.m. on February 17, Yu Zuomin ordered the companies to mobilize personnel to "protect" the headquarters and block the village entrances. Zhou Kewen, under Yu Zuomin's direction, was responsible for commanding the perimeter alert and patrol. Subsequently, tens of thousands of people unaware of the truth gathered in front of the headquarters building, and the main village entrances were blocked by trucks and oil tankers. Personnel armed with steel bars guarded the entrances and the area around the headquarters building day and night. On the morning of February 18, Yu Zuomin held a village-wide broadcast meeting, inciting all factories in the village to stop work and schools to close, thereby preventing the public security and procuratorial officers from carrying out their lawful duties.

Between late December 1992 and March 1993, defendants Yu Zuomin and Yu Shaozheng, in order to obtain state secrets related to the incidents in Daqiuzhuang, repeatedly bribed Gao Chao (handled in a separate case), a cadre of a certain Beijing agency. Yu Zuomin gave Gao Chao RMB 10,000, and Yu Shaozheng gave Gao Chao RMB 15,000. Gao Chao provided Yu Zuomin and Yu Shaozheng with three important classified state documents. Prior to this, in August 1992, Yu Zuomin, dissatisfied with the legal sentencing of villagers Yu Zuoxiang, Yu Zuoli, and five others for intentional injury, also bribed Gao Chao with USD 1,000, seeking his assistance with the relevant authorities.

The above facts regarding defendant Yu Zuomin's illegal control of others are confirmed by the statements of victims Yu Rongtian, Liu Jinhui, Liu Jingang, Liu Jingong, Liu Jinyun, and Liu Jinmin, as well as witness testimony. The facts regarding defendants Yu Zuomin, Yu Shaozheng, Liu Yonghua, Zhou Kewen, and Shi Jiaming's illegal detention of others are confirmed by the statements of victims Cheng Gang, Zhang Xinze, Tian Yizheng, Hou Hongbin, and Song Bao, as well as witness testimony and forensic medical examination reports. The facts regarding defendants Yu Zuomin, Liu Yonghua, Ma Deshui, Huang Naiqi, and Chen Guanghong's harboring of Liu Yunzhang, Li Zhenbiao, Chen Xiangqi, and Liu Shaosheng are confirmed by the confessions of the harbored individuals Liu Yunzhang and others, as well as other witness testimony. The facts regarding defendants Yu Zuomin and Zhou Kewen's obstruction of official duties are confirmed by witness testimony. The facts regarding defendants Yu Zuomin and Yu Shaozheng's bribery are confirmed by the confession of the bribe recipient Gao Chao, the testimony of Gao Chao's wife, and relevant documentary evidence. The eight defendants, including Yu Zuomin, also confessed to the main facts.

The Tianjin Intermediate People's Court held that: Defendant Yu Zuomin directed others to monitor the relatives of Liu Yutian and unlawfully restrict their personal freedom. His conduct violated Article 144 of the Criminal Law of the PRC and constituted the crime of illegal control. Given the serious circumstances of the crime, he should be given a heavier punishment. Yu Zuomin organized others to detain the teachers and students of the Cadre School and Tian Yizheng, Hou Hongbin, Song Bao, and others, unlawfully depriving them of their personal freedom. His conduct violated Article 143 of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of illegal detention. During the commission of the crime, he engaged in beating and humiliation, warranting a heavier punishment. Yu Zuomin directed others to harbor Liu Yunzhang and the other three criminals who beat Wei Fuhe to death. His conduct violated Article 162, paragraph 2, of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of harboring. The circumstances were serious, and he should be given a heavier punishment. Yu Zuomin ordered the detention of public security officers investigating the crime scene and organized and directed others to violently obstruct the lawful activities of public security and procuratorial officers in searching for criminals. His conduct violated Article 157 of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of obstruction of official duties. The circumstances were flagrant, and he should be given a heavier punishment. Yu Zuomin, together with defendant Yu Shaozheng, bribed a state functionary to obtain important state secrets. His conduct violated Article 7, paragraph 1, of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Punishment of Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery and constituted the crime of bribery. The circumstances were serious, and the punishment should be given a heavier punishment in accordance with Article 8, paragraph 1, of the Supplementary Provisions. Yu Zuomin's criminal conduct seriously undermined social order, so his political rights should also be deprived in accordance with Article 52 of the Criminal Law. In the crimes of illegal detention, harboring, and obstruction of official duties, Yu Zuomin played an organizational and directive role. In accordance with Articles 22 and 23 of the Criminal Law, he was a principal offender in joint intentional crimes and should be given a heavier punishment.

Defendant Yu Shaozheng participated in the criminal activities of illegally detaining the Cadre School teachers and students and Hou Hongbin and Song Bao. He played a secondary role in the joint crime and was an accessory to the crime of illegal detention. In accordance with Article 24 of the Criminal Law, he should be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offender. Yu Shaozheng, together with Yu Zuomin, harbored the criminal intent to spy on important state secrets. At Yu Zuomin's assignment, he went to Beijing to inquire about information related to this case and, to achieve the criminal purpose, bribed a state functionary with a large sum of money, then telegraphed the information obtained to Yu Zuomin. Yu Shaozheng's conduct constituted the crime of bribery and was a co-offender in the bribery.

Defendant Liu Yonghua, under the direction of Yu Zuomin, organized others and actively participated in the criminal activities of illegally detaining Tian Yizheng and Song Bao, and during the crimes engaged in beating and humiliation. Under the direction of Yu Zuomin, he actively organized others to harbor the criminals involved in the fatal beating of Wei Fuhe. He was a principal offender in the crimes of illegal detention and harboring and should be given a heavier punishment. However, after the incident, Liu Yonghua was able to confess to the main facts and expose accomplices, so he may be given a lighter punishment as appropriate.

Defendant Zhou Kewen, under the direction of Yu Zuomin, actively participated in the criminal activities of illegally detaining the Cadre School teachers and students and Tian Yizheng, Hou Hongbin, and Song Bao, and engaged in beating and humiliation. Under the direction of Yu Zuomin, he actively participated in and directed his subordinates to obstruct public security personnel from investigating the crime scene and to violently obstruct public security and procuratorial officers from searching for criminals. He was a principal offender in the crimes of illegal detention and obstruction of official duties and should be given a heavier punishment in accordance with the law.

The above four defendants, Yu Zuomin, Yu Shaozheng, Liu Yonghua, and Zhou Kewen, each committed multiple crimes and should be subject to concurrent punishment for multiple crimes in accordance with Article 64 of the Criminal Law.

Defendants Ma Deshui and Huang Naiqi, under the direction of Liu Yonghua, participated in harboring the criminals involved in the fatal beating of Wei Fuhe. Both played secondary roles in the crime of harboring and should be given lighter punishments compared to the principal offender.

Defendant Chen Guanghong, knowing that Chen Xiangqi, whom Liu Yonghua was organizing to harbor, was a wanted criminal, still contacted Liu Yonghua to arrange a vehicle and transported Chen Xiangqi to another location to hide. He was an accessory in the crime of harboring and should be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offender.

Defendant Shi Jiaming participated in the criminal activities of illegally detaining the Cadre School teachers and students and Tian Yizheng, Hou Hongbin, and Song Bao, and engaged in beating and humiliation. She should be given a heavier punishment in accordance with the law. However, Shi Jiaming played a secondary role in the joint crime of illegal detention and was an accessory, so she should be given a lighter punishment compared to the principal offender. Shi Jiaming voluntarily surrendered, and in accordance with Article 63 of the Criminal Law, she may be given a lighter punishment.

In accordance with the above, the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on August 27, 1993:

The defendant Yu Zuomin was sentenced to three years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of illegal control; three years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of illegal detention; six years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of harboring; three years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of obstruction of official duties; ten years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of bribery, with deprivation of political rights for two years. The combined sentence was fixed-term imprisonment of twenty years, with deprivation of political rights for two years.

The defendant Yu Shaozheng was sentenced to two years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of illegal detention; nine years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of bribery. The combined sentence was fixed-term imprisonment of ten years.

The defendant Liu Yonghua was sentenced to two years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of illegal detention; four years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of harboring. The combined sentence was fixed-term imprisonment of four years.

The defendant Zhou Kewen was sentenced to three years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of illegal detention; two years and six months' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of obstruction of official duties. The combined sentence was fixed-term imprisonment of five years.

The defendant Ma Deshui was sentenced to three years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of harboring.

The defendant Huang Naiqi was sentenced to three years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of harboring.

The defendant Chen Guanghong was sentenced to two years' fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of harboring.

The defendant Shi Jiaming was sentenced to one year's fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of illegal detention.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, defendant Yu Shaozheng appealed to the Tianjin High People's Court, on the grounds that "the bribe of RMB 25,000 given to Gao Chao was solely my own act, unrelated to Yu Zuomin, and was not a joint crime with Yu Zuomin; during the detention of Cheng Gang and Zhang Xinze, I did not slap Zhang Xinze, and the perforation of Zhang Xinze's eardrum was unrelated to me."

After trial, the Tianjin High People's Court held that: The fact that Yu Zuomin bribed Gao Chao with RMB 10,000 and USD 1,000 was not only confessed by Yu Zuomin but also corroborated by Gao Chao's confession. The appellant Yu Shaozheng's claim that the bribery of Gao Chao was solely his own act was clearly an attempt to exonerate Yu Zuomin, and this ground of appeal was untenable. Defendants Zhou Kewen and Shi Jiaming, who were present at the scene of the beating of Zhang Xinze, both testified that it was Yu Shaozheng who slapped Zhang Xinze. The victim Zhang Xinze, upon identification, also confirmed that Yu Shaozheng slapped him, causing the eardrum perforation. Yu Shaozheng's appeal statement that he did not slap Zhang Xinze was a pure fabrication. None of Yu Shaozheng's grounds of appeal were accepted. The criminal facts of the other defendants as found in the original trial were also clear, and the evidence was indeed sufficient. In light of the criminal facts, circumstances, roles in the joint crimes, and attitudes toward confession of the appellant and defendants, the convictions and sentences in the original trial were appropriate and should be affirmed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 136, item (1), of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, the Tianjin High People's Court rendered a final ruling on September 10, 1993: Reject the appeal and affirm the original judgment.
